the FEL amplification process of a 266 nm input signal will be tested at SPARC in two different configurations: (i) a single-pass FEL with an undulator length of 1.8 m; (ii) a cascaded FEL with two undulators, each 1.8m long, separated by a 3.2 m drift.
the amplification and generation of higher harmonic signals can be obtained in SPARC FEL, and that the amplification process can be optimized by tuning the FEL parameters.
the SPARC FELS will be used to test the seeding process in cascaded FELs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the amplification process and the FEL gain of a seeded input signal in a free electron laser.
the development of the FEL seeding technique and the improvement of the FEL performances in the UV and soft x-ray regions.
the development of a FEL source based on a seed signal that will allow to increase the FEL efficiency, to reduce the FEL pulse duration and to increase the FWHM bandwidth of the emitted radiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SPARC facility can be used to test the FEL harmonic cascade process with the possibility to generate the seed signal at 266 nm in gases or at 400 nm in crystals.
the FEL seeding experiments will allow to study the amplification of the input signal in a wide spectral range (266 nm,160 nm, 400 nm, 114 n m).
the SPARC FHEL is an ideal facility to test FEL harmonic generation in the UV and X-ray range, with an excellent potential for the development of future FEL seeded sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we will study the amplification process of a seed signal in an FEL amplifier and the harmonic generation of a seed signal by the FEL radiation in a cascaded scheme.
the DS4 EURO FEL collaboration aims to test the amplification of a seed pulse generated by a high-order harmonic source and to investigate the FEL harmonic generations in a cascaded scheme.
the DS4 EURO FEL programme will allow to test and validate the FEL harmonic seeding technique in the UV and VUV range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SPARC FELS can be used to demonstrate the feasibility of the FEL seeding concept, paving the way to the realization of a seeded FEL source in the 50-100 nm spectral region.
a seed laser can be used as a powerful tool to tune the FEL output wavelength and intensity.
the SPARC FEC is an excellent tool to test and study the seeding of FELs with a seed signal generated in crystals, gases or both.
